mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility rose monotonically from 5.3 to 10.0 percent above baseline across the four weeks and closed at its window maximum, showing households still shifting time from out-of-home to home. That substitution keeps draining discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC averages lower over the next 28 days than its trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose 5.3 -> 9.1 -> 7.0 -> 10.0 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is greater than or equal to the last 28-day mean (-31.8) while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 8.0 percent above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT closed at -23.4 percent, below the -20 threshold, after oscillating between -10.4 and -24.1. A sub-threshold transit level means transit-dependent discretionary trips are being abandoned, so retail catchments served by transit corridors lose traffic and RETAIL_REC prints below its trailing four-week mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean falls below -20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT t-0w = -23.4, the second lowest of the four weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days averages above -31.8 in instances where TRANSIT stayed below -20 for the full preceding fortnight.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-23.4) and WORKPLACES (-26.3) are jointly depressed at the decision point, so the commute corridor and the transit link into retail districts are cut at the same time. The compounding loss of weekday footfall drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks by more than either series alone predicts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both below -20 percent change from baseline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series hit their window lows at t-2w and again at t-0w
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both below -20, the next 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is not lower than the next 14-day mean observed when only one of the two is below -20.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC oscillates on a two-week beat (-26.3, -35.3, -30.1, -35.6) and closed at a fresh four-week low of -35.6. Trough prints of that depth are followed by a partial rebound week as deferred errands are executed, so the next four-week mean exceeds the trailing mean of -31.8.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly mean prints at or below -35.0, a new four-week low
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC alternated high-low-high-low and t-0w = -35.6 is the window minimum
failure_condition: Following a week with RETAIL_REC at or below -35.0, the next 14-day mean is lower than the four-week mean that preceded the trough in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS at -31.1 together with RESIDENTIAL at 10.0 marks the mid-winter seasonal trough of out-of-home activity. As the seasonal low passes, discretionary spending rotates back indoors, so RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks averages above its trailing four-week mean of -31.8.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS t-0w = -31.1 equals the window minimum of -31.0 to within 0.1 point
failure_condition: In the four weeks after a PARKS print at or below -30 with RESIDENTIAL at or above 9.0, RETAIL_REC averages at or below its trailing four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, WORKPLACES at -26.3 combined with GROCERY_PHARM holding near baseline (-0.9) shows discretionary venues are closed while essential retail stays open. Because the constraint targets non-essential capacity directly, RETAIL_REC keeps falling over four weeks while grocery traffic is preserved.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -25 while GROCERY_PHARM remains above -5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM recovered to -0.9 while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT struck new lows at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES is below -25 and GROCERY_PHARM is above -5, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not below the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM jumped from -7.6 to -0.9 in the latest week, a precautionary stockpiling signal. Households that rebuild pantry stocks cut discretionary shopping trips immediately afterward, so RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days sits below the -35.6 print of the decision week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises by 5 points or more versus the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved -7.6 (t-2w) to 2.4 (t-1w) to -0.9 (t-0w), a 6.7-point week-on-week rise at t-0w
failure_condition: Following a week-on-week GROCERY_PHARM rise of 5 points or more, RETAIL_REC in the subsequent 7 days is not lower than its value in the triggering week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each post a second consecutive weekly improvement of at least 5 points, restrictions are easing and commuting-derived retail footfall returns to storefronts. RETAIL_REC then averages higher over the next 14 days than its trailing four-week mean, with the two series reinforcing each other rather than moving independently.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each improve by 5 points or more versus the prior week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved by roughly 8 points from t-2w to t-1w, the only rebound week in the window
failure_condition: After two consecutive joint 5-point gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the following 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or below the preceding four-week mean.
